platform: native Linux/amd64; Go 1.26.5 cross-compiled on Windows; CGO disabled
checks: new application starts/migrates with original retention policy, stored key/login, node membership and public privacy
actual deployed-image Agent authenticates and reports via websocket/v1 without false configuration confirmation
actual authenticated encrypted HTTP export persisted to private file
large archive uploaded as bounded multipart and durably staged with CSRF/session
full new Server restart applies pending restore, preserves previous database and exact ordered report digest, excludes post-backup marker and permits fresh stored-login authentication
pre-backup deployed Agent credential authenticates and stores new reports after actual application restore
actual previous deployed Server starts on separate original-schema copy with original stored key/login and original node membership

prior_attempts.reason: sysfs interface view guard; stopped before copies or application startup
previous application HTTP readiness exceeded the initial 150-second observation deadline; no success result written

scope: same-host isolated loopback copies; actual deployed executables, stored key/login, HTTP encrypted export/stage/restart and old-application rollback; no public traffic switch, external OAuth/Provider or cross-machine large-database claim
limitations: Roundtrip copy alone uses 3650-day tier retention for exact snapshot comparison; original settings were tested separately.
Previous application uses a separate original-schema copy, never the migrated database. Its normal synchronous retention still runs.
Resource controls and observed startup times are not a whole-machine capacity, RSS or old/new performance benchmark.
Only screened aggregate metadata is published. Private backups, runtime keys, login data, row data, archive passphrase and process logs remain off-repository.
